title: Prema Yadav v. State of U.P.
coram: Vivek Chaudhary, J.; Om Prakash Shukla, J.
disposition: Writ disposed of with liberty to apply to the CGRF under Electricity Supply Code clause 7.10(3), including a stay application to be considered expeditiously.
headnote: A writ of certiorari to quash a 31 January 2024 electricity order was disposed of because the consumer had an alternative remedy of applying under Section 7.10 sub-clause (3) of the Electricity Supply Code to the Consumer Redressal Forum, with a stay application which that Forum would consider expeditiously.
facts: Prema Yadav petitioned the Lucknow Bench of the Allahabad High Court for a writ of certiorari to quash an order dated 31 January 2024 passed by respondent no. 3, an officer under the State Energy Department. Counsel for respondents 2 to 4, the distribution-licensee interests, submitted that the petitioner had an alternative remedy of applying under Section 7.10 sub-clause (3) of the Electricity Supply Code to the Consumer Redressal Forum, together with a stay application, which the Forum would consider expeditiously.

holding_units.holding: A writ of certiorari against an electricity order dated 31.01.2024 is not entertained where the consumer has an alternative remedy of filing an application under Section 7.10 sub-clause (3) of the Electricity Supply Code before the Consumer Redressal Forum, together with a stay application which the Forum shall consider expeditiously; the petition is disposed of with liberty to avail that remedy.
holding_units.flag: Court cited 'Section 7.10 sub-clause (3)' of the Electricity Supply Code (catalog analogue UP-2005::7.10(iii)).

principle_tags.application: The Division Bench accepted that certiorari against the 31 January 2024 order must yield to an application and stay under clause 7.10(3) before the Consumer Redressal Forum, and disposed of the writ with liberty to that forum.

not_decided.point: Merits of the impugned order dated 31.01.2024
not_decided.note: The writ was disposed of on alternative remedy without examining the order under challenge.
